body.target_estimand: The observed-law target is \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) for \(a\in J\). Under the frozen model this functional is not identified with \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]\) uniformly over full-data witnesses; an additional condition linking realized-dose consistency to deterministic-dose sections is required for that causal equality.

sampling_model.design: The observed sample is iid from \(P\in\mathcal M\). Although membership requires at least one full-data extension satisfying consistency, sectionwise conditional exchangeability, and conditional-potential-mean continuity, those conditions do not force all admissible extensions to agree on \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The frozen description names boundary-corrected local-polynomial learners with bandwidth \(n^{-1/(2s)}\), but it does not yet specify a complete sample map. The stated exponents are conditional on a regular compactly supported kernel, uniformly invertible boundary moment equations, a density-normalization map, and a singular-Gram convention; the required validation-fold stochastic bound remains open.
sampling_model.overlap: The conditional treatment density \(g(a\mid w)\) is bounded above and away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: The dose \(A_i\in[0,1]\) is continuous, and profiling is restricted to the interior interval \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\).
sampling_model.units: The iid observations are \(O_i=(W_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with compact covariates and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The limiting distribution is the integral of the difference of the squared constrained and unconstrained slope processes.
We study the extremal behavior of the stationary argmax process on increasing intervals.
A suitably standardized supremum of the Grenander-type estimation error converges to a standard Gumbel random variable.
The confidence intervals concern the continuous treatment effect curve at a fixed point and invert a likelihood-ratio-type test.
The paper provides general conditions for consistency and pointwise convergence of generalized Grenander-type estimators.
Approximation results for the supremum of an empirical process yield asymptotically valid uniform confidence bands.
The paper develops a bootstrap procedure for constructing uniform confidence bands from weighted local-linear estimation.

body.tldr: The frozen assumptions do not identify the exact-dose causal curve, and the Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio excursion law required for simultaneous calibration remains open. The completed mathematics is narrower: fixed-location finite-dimensional stationarity, exact Brownian dilation, the deterministic action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\) with an explicit plateau witness, conditional nuisance and transfer algebra, the spatial-volume clock, conditional centering calculus, and deterministic profile inversion. The construction is therefore an observed-law likelihood-ratio profiling architecture, not a calibrated simultaneous causal band or a validated Gumbel procedure.

project_justification.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) provide the fixed-location Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio functional. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) analyze a distinct Markov argmax process, and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) analyze slope-error extremes. None supplies the infinite-domain GCM contact-set large-deviation principle, minimizer classification, sharp Palm expansion, anticlustering, marked-Poisson approximation, or continuum-grid theorem needed here. Separately, the frozen causal assumptions admit observed-equivalent full-data extensions with different exact-dose causal means.
project_justification.niche: The actionable research niche is an open-problem program: repair exact-dose causal identification, establish the Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio-energy contact-set excursion mechanism, and then prove uniform transfer to the optimized observed statistic. The current deterministic action and spatial-clock calculations identify the relevant objects without supplying the missing probability law.
project_justification.fill: The completed results provide exact Brownian/GCM dilation, the action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\), an explicit plateau witness, finite-dimensional stationarity, conditional nuisance-rate and transfer algebra, the exact spatial clock, conditional centering substitution, profile interval structure, crossing-set containment, and homogeneous reduction. The infinite-domain large-deviation, Palm, anticlustering, marked-Poisson, continuum transfer, simulation, and coverage steps remain open.

body.related_work: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) are used only for the finite fixed-location Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio functional. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) obtain extremes for a different Markov argmax process with explicit transition machinery; Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) transfer slope-error extremes, not likelihood-ratio-energy excursions. Doss (2026) supplies neighboring fixed-dose causal-isotonic likelihood-ratio work, while Takatsu and Westling (2025), Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026), and Doss--VandenBerg develop neighboring simultaneous-band approaches. The present results neither tighten those probability theorems nor establish optimal width, tuning freedom, or dominance over the Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact identity \(\Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}\) determines the small-noise scaling, and the deterministic action lies between \(1/2\) and \(9/8\). No infinite-domain large-deviation principle connects that action to a logarithmic tail. Even such a logarithmic equivalent would not provide the bounded-level tail ratio or sharp Palm prefactor. Missing ingredients are contact-set exponential tightness and continuity, action-minimizer classification and uniqueness modulo translation, transverse fluctuation and multiplicity analysis, conditional cluster-shape control, short-range anticlustering, marked-Poisson approximation, and a sample-path modulus/grid theorem. Statistically, the learner is not yet a single fully specified sample map, and optimized likelihood-ratio transfer still lacks the required fitted-kernel maximal inequality, common localization, and slope envelope.
body.honest_scope: No exact-dose causal identification theorem, sharp likelihood-ratio excursion theorem, growing-domain coupling, feasible Gumbel calibration, simulated-grid approximation, or nominal simultaneous coverage theorem is proved. The profile threshold remains arbitrary, and deterministic inversion preserves only the probability of its common likelihood-ratio event. The contact-set excursion mechanism is an explicit open question that is not consumed by a current proved theorem. No claim is made about optimal width, tuning freedom, or dominance over the Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.interpretation: The estimand \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) is an observed-law G-computation curve on \(J\). Under the frozen assumptions it is not uniformly equal to the exact-dose causal mean. For the AHA/CMS nurse-hours--readmission application, the current mathematics supports an observed-law isotonic likelihood-ratio profile and a deterministic map from any common profile event to threshold-crossing sets; it does not support reporting those sets as calibrated simultaneous causal confidence sets.
